quick.summary: Why building instant data pipelines is often a waste of resources.
quick.takeaway: Only send data instantly if the business acts on it instantly.

beats.line: I built an instant data stream for orders. Nobody uses it. Why?
Think of laundry. You do not wash one shirt at a time.
You wait for a full basket to save effort.
So I am washing single shirts with my data?
Yes. Moving data instantly is costly. We call it event driven integration.
Can I just say sending it instantly?
Yes. Only send it instantly if the business acts instantly.
The warehouse only packs boxes once a day.
So they just need a daily batch of orders.
I will switch to a daily upload to save money.
Match the speed of data to the speed of work.

quiz.question: When should you spend the resources to move data instantly?
options: When the business process acts on it immediately.
Whenever you want to build a modern pipeline.
When the system has more than one user.
When the data volume is very low.
quiz.explanation: Sending data instantly is expensive. It is only worth the cost if the business takes action in real time.

quiz.question: Sending a daily batch of records is always a bad design choice.
quiz.explanation: Batch processing is highly efficient. It is often the best choice if the business only updates work once a day.
